b1-3and.title: Possession: Andi, Andak, Ando...
b1-3and.pattern: عندي / عندك / عنده / عندا / عندنا / عندكن / عندن
b1-3and.explanation: Arabic has no verb "to have" — Syrian uses عند (3and, literally "at/by") fused with a person ending: عندي (3andi, "I have"), عندك (3andak, "you-m have"), عنده (3ando, "he has"), عندا (3anda, "she has"), عندنا (3andna, "we have"), عندكن (3andkon, "you-all have"), عندن (3andon, "they have"). Negate it with ما: ما عندي (ma 3andi, "I don't have").
b1-3and.fact: عند marks lasting/permanent possession (owning something), distinct from مع (ma3, "with") used for what you're physically carrying right now — a nuance English's single word "have" doesn't capture.

dialogue.en: Yes, I have money, thank God

b1-lian.title: Because: Lأan and Ashan
b1-lian.explanation: لأن (la2an) and عشان (3ashan) both mean "because" and are largely interchangeable in everyday Syrian speech: أنا منيح اليوم لأن شفت الأهل ("I'm good today because I saw the family") or أنا منيح اليوم عشان شفت الأهل — either works.
b1-lian.fact: عشان also does double duty as "in order to" before a verb, not just "because" before a full clause — a small extra flexibility لأن doesn't share.
